priors.title: EXAFS Structural Determination of the Pt2(P2O5H2)44– Anion in Solution
priors.snippet: A Pt–Pt distance of 2.876(28) Å and a Pt–P bond length of 2.32(4) Å are obtained.

priors.title: Quantitative measurement of the reduction of platinum(iv) complexes using X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES)
priors.snippet: Reduction of Pt(IV) complexes over time in cell growth media and A2780 cells was observed by XANES, and shown to correspond with their reduction potentials and cytotoxicities.

priors.title: Fitting EXAFS data using molecular dynamics outputs and a histogram approach
priors.snippet: The estimation of metal nanoparticle diameter by analysis of extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data from coordination numbers is nontrivial, particularly for particles 5 nm in diameter, for which the undercoordination of surface atoms becomes an increasingly significant contribution to the average coordination number.

priors.title: Pt nanoparticles dispersed in a metal-organic framework as peroxidase mimics for colorimetric detection of GSH
priors.snippet: We successfully synthesized Pt@ZIF-8 in two steps, the average particle size of Pt nanoparticles is about 3 nm.

priors.title: Thermodynamic properties of Pt nanoparticles: Size, shape, support, and adsorbate effects
priors.snippet: For large NP sizes (diameter $d$ >1.5 nm) \ensuremath{\Theta}${}_{D}$ was found to decrease toward \ensuremath{\Theta}${}_{D}$ of bulk Pt with increasing NP size.

priors.title: Size effects on reactivity of Pt nanoparticles in CO monolayer oxidation: The role of surface mobility
priors.snippet: Significant size effects are observed in the particle size interval from ca. 1 to 4 nm, including the positive shift of the CO stripping peak with decreasing particle size and a pronounced asymmetry of the current transients at constant potential.

priors.title: Pt nanoparticle stability in PEM fuel cells: influence of particle size distribution and crossover hydrogen
priors.snippet: Our model demonstrates that, due to rapid changes in the Gibbs–Thomson energy, particle size effects dominate degradation for ∼2 nm particles but play almost no role for ∼5 nm particles.
